fixes.explanation: Paul says it plain: “…you should have commended me…” He says they drove him to being a fool, so a little credit was in order. I'd want a pat on the hat myself in that spot.
Yes, friend. Paul writes, “…since I am in no way inferior to those “super-apostles,” even though I am nothing.” Both claims sit in the same sentence. That's a lot to fit into one breath.
Not quite, friend. Paul writes, “…I am in no way inferior to those “super-apostles,”…” He says it flat out. Right after that he adds, “…even though I am nothing.”
That's the list, baker. Paul says “…signs, wonders, and miracles…” were performed among them. He adds that they were done with great perseverance. The Corinthians were right there among it.

Those are good things, friend, but Paul doesn't list them in this verse. Fasting and prayer didn't make this list, and I would have bet my apron on them too. What he says is that “…signs, wonders, and miracles…” were performed among the Corinthians.

Yes, baker. Paul asks, “In what way were you inferior to the other churches, except that I was not a burden to you?” So the one difference he names is that he didn't burden them. Then he adds, “Forgive me this wrong!” I think that line has a twinkle in it.

Right, baker. Paul says, “For children should not have to save up for their parents, but parents for their children.” The saving goes from parents to children. Just before that he says he is “…not seeking your possessions, but you.”

Paul doesn't bring brothers and sisters into this one, friend. Nobody's splitting a cookie jar between siblings here. He says, “For children should not have to save up for their parents, but parents for their children.” So the saving goes from parents to children.
A house is a big thing to give, and I'd have guessed it too. But Paul doesn't mention one. The verse says, “…I will most gladly spend my money and myself.” Not a deed or a key in sight.
That's him, baker. Paul names Titus as the one he urged to visit them. Titus is Paul's partner and fellow worker (2 Corinthians 8:23). Right after that, Paul asks if Titus exploited them in any way.
Right, baker. Paul asks, “Did we not walk in the same Spirit and follow in the same footsteps?” Same Spirit, same footsteps. That's his point about himself and Titus.

That's not what Paul says, friend. He asks, “Did we not walk in the same Spirit and follow in the same footsteps?” His point is that he and Titus walked alike. Nothing about a separate plan is in the verse.
Sorting things out sounds tidy, and I'd love a tidy bakery myself, but those aren't Paul's words. He says, “…all of this, beloved, is to build you up.” Building up is the word he picked.

That's on the list, baker. Paul says, “I fear that there may be quarreling, jealousy, rage, rivalry, slander, gossip, arrogance, and disorder.” You picked three of the eight. He fears they may be there when he comes, and every one of them is about how people treat each other.

That's the word, baker. Paul says, “I am afraid that when I come again, my God will humble me before you…” It's a fear, not a sure thing. He adds that he will be grieved over many who have sinned earlier.

Giving came up earlier in this passage, friend, so I get why it's tempting. But Paul says he fears he will be grieved over many who have sinned earlier and have not repented. Right passage, wrong word.
Gathering isn't what Paul says here, baker. He fears he will be grieved over many who sinned earlier and “…have not repented…” Repented is the word, and it's a heavy one.
